Computers and phones on the same Wi-Fi or tailnet can then open this phone's terminal with a link that carries its own access token.

Anyone who has the link can run commands here as the Gecko app: read and change its files and use the network. Not other apps' data, not your photos and documents (Gecko has no storage permission), and nothing that needs root.

Gecko only answers private addresses (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Tailscale), and only with the link. Turn it off when you're done: the link stops working, and the next one is new.

This phone\'s public key. Add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on a machine to log in there without a password, from the terminal on this phone (ssh) and when you add the machine to Gecko. Its private key stays in the app.
Couldn\'t make this phone\'s SSH key: %1$s
To reach you while the phone sleeps, Gecko\'s background connection needs to be left out of battery optimization. Gecko only keeps one small connection open.
Battery optimization already leaves Gecko alone.
On Samsung phones: Settings, Apps, Gecko, Battery: Unrestricted. Also make sure Gecko isn\'t in Battery, Background usage limits, Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones: turn on Autostart for Gecko, and set Battery saver to No restrictions (Settings, Apps, Gecko). Locking Gecko in the recent apps helps too.
On OnePlus phones: Settings, Apps, Gecko, Battery: allow background activity and set it to Unrestricted (or Don\'t optimize). Turn on Auto launch if your phone has it.
On Oppo and Realme phones: allow Auto launch for Gecko, and in Settings, Apps, Gecko, Battery: allow background activity.
On Vivo and iQOO phones: allow Gecko to run in the background (Battery, Background power consumption) and turn on Autostart.
On Huawei and Honor phones: Settings, Battery, App launch: set Gecko to Manage manually and turn on Auto launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
This phone\'s Android System WebView is version %1$s. Gecko needs version 111 or newer (Android keeps it up to date from the Play Store).

Gecko runs in Termux as a background task (Termux\'s notification counts it). It keeps running while you use other apps, and shows up as a machine in This phone\'s sidebar; stop it from the ⋮ menu next to This phone.

Termux is a Linux environment for Android with its own packages: git, tmux, Node, Python, Go, ssh and more. Gecko runs inside it, and Termux becomes one of This phone\'s machines: its tabs and agents sit next to the phone\'s own, with notifications and the extra keys.\n\nGet Termux from F-Droid or from its GitHub releases, then come back.

The Termux on Google Play is a separate build that takes no commands from other apps, so the app can\'t start Gecko there. Gecko does run in it: install it with Gecko\'s Termux installer, run gecko there, and add its link on This phone (+ next to Machines, Paste a Gecko link). For Gecko to start it from here, use Termux from F-Droid or GitHub. Termux builds from different places can\'t be mixed: their add-ons have to come from the same place.
Let Gecko start commands in Termux

Gecko starts and stops its daemon in Termux, and asks it for its link, with Termux\'s permission \"Run commands in Termux environment\". Android asks you once.\n\nIt can run any command in Termux, as Termux. Gecko uses it only for gecko itself.
Allow it in the app\'s settings
Android won\'t ask again. In Gecko\'s app info, open Permissions, then the additional permissions, and allow \"Run commands in Termux environment\".
Allow apps in Termux, and install Gecko
Termux takes commands from other apps only when you allow it. Open Termux and run this line: it installs Gecko there (or updates it) and allows the Gecko app.

Open Termux once, so Android lets it run, then try again. If it still doesn\'t answer, make sure Android doesn\'t restrict Termux\'s battery use.
Termux works. Gecko isn\'t installed in it yet: this line installs it (no root needed). Run it in a Termux session, or let the app send it there.
